investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so no pod ever reached a running state and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, the agent pod never starts, the VM is never assigned, and the eval runner receives no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]). This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 127s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied without a scheduled pod.
source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three remote-agent checks share the same swarm-backed VM provisioning path, explaining why all three fail with the same scheduler message.
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes in the production cluster, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary: The pod's node affinity or node selector is too restrictive, limiting scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes. If the affinity were relaxed or additional nodes were labeled, more capacity would be available.
Tertiary: A concurrent workload or a previously created remote-agent pod that was not cleaned up is holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new allocations.
Lower probability: A node or VM provider quota change reduced the advertised kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes without a corresponding scale-out of the node pool.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the production Kubernetes cluster for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes using 'kubectl describe nodes'. If both nodes are at capacity, scale out the node pool or terminate any leaked remote-agent pods to free the resource.

Audit the withCleanup path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm that remote-agent pods are reliably deleted after each eval run. Leaked pods from prior failed runs are a plausible cause of sustained resource exhaustion.

Review the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity and selector to determine whether the eligible node pool (currently 2 of 6 nodes) can be safely expanded by labeling additional nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or relaxing the affinity.

Once cluster capacity is restored, re-run the eval (AURA_STATUS_RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT=production-api AURA_STATUS_CHECKS=remote-agent-create npm run status:probes) to confirm that vmIdPresent and remoteState evidence are collected and the contract passes.
Consider adding a cluster-level alert for kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization approaching 100% on eligible nodes so capacity exhaustion is detected before it causes eval failures.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > used) on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.
If the scheduler message were absent from a re-run and the pod reached Pending or Running state, the issue would be transient and not a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only one of the three remote-agent checks failed while the others passed, a shared infrastructure capacity cause would be less likely and a check-specific configuration or cleanup bug would be more likely.

If the pod spec for the remote-agent type did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as an extended resource, the scheduler message would implicate a different resource or affinity misconfiguration rather than VM capacity.

If a passing run were found in history (lastPassingAt is currently null per verifierContext.history), it would indicate a regression rather than a persistent misconfiguration, and the timing of that regression would need to be correlated with cluster events.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the pod-stuck timeout.
Add an eval that verifies the withCleanup path successfully deletes remote-agent pods after each run, to detect resource leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Add a cluster resource headroom eval that asserts kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable minus used is above a minimum threshold on the eligible node pool, running on a shorter interval than the remote-agent-create check.

Add a historical baseline eval that tracks lastPassingAt for remote-agent-create and alerts if no passing run has been recorded within a configurable window, enabling earlier detection of persistent scheduling failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T19:52–19:57Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, and state all missing), violating its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no node could accept the eval pod, so createAgent never returned, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a user-facing API outage confirmed by traffic signals.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on both eligible nodes with no preemption victims available, making this the primary and most directly evidenced cause.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: 4 nodes are structurally excluded from scheduling this pod type, reducing the effective pool to 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure on those 2 nodes.

Concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads did not release VM slots (e.g., due to failed cleanup), the resource pool could be depleted without new demand.

Cluster autoscaler not provisioning additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time: the 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' message indicates the scheduler found no path to free capacity, which could mean autoscaling is disabled, slow, or not configured for this node pool.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption path was available, so no pod ever reached a running state and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, the agent pod never starts, the VM is never assigned, and the eval runner receives no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running, idle, ready]). This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 127s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable root message, pod stuck for 146s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion and affinity mismatch.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root message, pod stuck for 147s, same resource exhaustion.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the pod never reached a state where the runner could collect VM or agent identity data.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned a schedulable pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which must schedule a kata peer-pod; if that pod is Unschedulable the runner cannot proceed to collect vmIdPresent or remoteState.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied without a scheduled pod.
source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three remote-agent checks share the same swarm-backed VM provisioning path, explaining why all three fail with the same scheduler message.
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes in the production cluster, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary: The pod's node affinity or node selector is too restrictive, limiting scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes. If the affinity were relaxed or additional nodes were labeled, more capacity would be available.
Tertiary: A concurrent workload or a previously created remote-agent pod that was not cleaned up is holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new allocations.
Lower probability: A node or VM provider quota change reduced the advertised kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes without a corresponding scale-out of the node pool.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available (allocatable > used) on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.
If the scheduler message were absent from a re-run and the pod reached Pending or Running state, the issue would be transient and not a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If only one of the three remote-agent checks failed while the others passed, a shared infrastructure capacity cause would be less likely and a check-specific configuration or cleanup bug would be more likely.

If the pod spec for the remote-agent type did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as an extended resource, the scheduler message would implicate a different resource or affinity misconfiguration rather than VM capacity.

If a passing run were found in history (lastPassingAt is currently null per verifierContext.history), it would indicate a regression rather than a persistent misconfiguration, and the timing of that regression would need to be correlated with cluster events.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the pod-stuck timeout.
Add an eval that verifies the withCleanup path successfully deletes remote-agent pods after each run, to detect resource leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Add a cluster resource headroom eval that asserts kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable minus used is above a minimum threshold on the eligible node pool, running on a shorter interval than the remote-agent-create check.

Add a historical baseline eval that tracks lastPassingAt for remote-agent-create and alerts if no passing run has been recorded within a configurable window, enabling earlier detection of persistent scheduling failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod spawned by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. No evidence was collected by any check, confirming the agent VM never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints on the remote-agent pod spec. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime chat from completing. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that triggers pod scheduling and would block indefinitely if the pod cannot be scheduled
possibleCauses: Primary: The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have reached their maximum peer-pod VM quota (e.g., all VM slots are occupied by existing running agents or leaked pods), leaving no capacity for new eval pods.
Secondary: A recent increase in concurrent remote-agent usage or a prior eval run left pods in a non-terminated state, consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and blocking new scheduling.

Tertiary: The 4 non-kata nodes are excluded by a node affinity or nodeSelector on the remote-agent pod spec that requires kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning the effective schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

Lower confidence: A node-level issue (e.g., node NotReady, kubelet failure, or resource pressure) on the 2 kata-capable nodes could have reduced their reported allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm count to zero without actual VM exhaustion — this would require kubectl describe node output to distinguish.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable message if capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources in the target namespace to identify capacity consumers
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl to list pods in the remote-agents namespace and filter for those using the kata runtime class or peer-pod annotations. Look for Running, Pending, or Terminating pods that are holding VM slots.

reproductionSteps.label: Describe the 2 kata-capable nodes to inspect allocatable and allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm counts
reproductionSteps.details: Run kubectl describe node on each of the 2 nodes that report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm. Check the Allocatable and Allocated resources sections for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs
reproductionSteps.details: List all pods in the remote-agents namespace that are not in a terminal state (Succeeded or Failed). Pods left running by prior eval runs or by cleanup failures would consume VM slots.

reproductionSteps.label: Run the sibling checks in sequence to confirm all three checks reproduce the same scheduler error
reproductionSteps.details: All three checks should reproduce the Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm as the exhausted resource on the 2 eligible nodes. All three remote-agents checks failed with this same constraint, localizing the failure to the VM scheduling layer for remote agent pods.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create check (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check remote-agent-create failed with the same Unschedulable message (evidence id: sibling.remote-agent-create), confirming agent creation is blocked at the scheduling step.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-state check (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check remote-agent-state failed with the same Unschedulable message (evidence id: sibling.remote-agent-state), confirming state polling is also blocked because no agent pod can be created.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime check (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The primary failing check. The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers pod scheduling. The pod was stuck Unschedulable for 147s before the check failed.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — degraded state threshold
affectedAreas.reason: features.json line 187 sets degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2. With all 3 checks failing (2 required: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state), the feature is at or past the outage threshold for required checks.
affectedAreas.details: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes with kubectl describe node to determine current allocatable vs. allocated VM slot counts and identify what is consuming capacity.

List all pods in the remote-agents namespace that are in Running or Pending state to find any leaked pods from prior eval runs or live workloads consuming VM slots. Terminate any pods that should have been cleaned up.

If VM slots are genuinely exhausted by live workloads, assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on those nodes can be increased or whether additional kata-capable nodes can be added to the cluster.
Review the withCleanup function in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm it reliably terminates remote-agent pods after each eval run, preventing slot leakage across runs.

Confirm the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec to understand why 4 of 6 nodes are permanently ineligible. If those nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the kata runtime class), the schedulable pool would grow from 2 to 6 nodes.

Monitor the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state checks (both marked required=true in features.json line 183-184) as the feature is at or past the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold for required checks.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect allocatable and allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 eligible nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether VM slots are exhausted or whether the node is reporting zero capacity due to a node condition. This is the single most important probe to run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all non-terminal pods in the remote-agents namespace to find capacity consumers
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether prior eval runs, leaked pods, or concurrent workloads are holding all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, which would confirm the exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the failed expected-output contract after confirming or clearing capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies whether the failure is reproducible (sustained exhaustion) or transient. A pass after capacity is freed confirms the root cause.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check Kubernetes events for the stuck pods in the remote-agents namespace
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: kubectl get events filtered to the remote-agents namespace and the eval run timestamp will show the exact scheduler rejection reason and whether preemption was attempted, corroborating or refining the evidence in failed-check.message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity and nodeSelector on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms why 4 of 6 nodes are ineligible, establishing the true schedulable pool size and whether the affinity constraint can be relaxed to increase capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots greater than zero, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, label mismatch, or quota policy) would need to be investigated.
If the eval runner's withCleanup function is confirmed to have successfully terminated all prior remote-agent pods before this run, leaked pods would be ruled out as the capacity consumer.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are shown to also carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource but are excluded by an unrelated affinity rule, the effective schedulable pool size would need to be re-evaluated separately from the VM capacity question.
If a subsequent eval run immediately after this one succeeds without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If node-level events show the 2 kata nodes were in NotReady or MemoryPressure state at the time of the eval, the reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm could reflect a node condition rather than true VM slot exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks the current allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm count across all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity signal rather than waiting for a pod scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that counts non-terminal remote-agent pods in the namespace before and after each eval run to detect cleanup failures and slot leakage.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies at least N kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available across the cluster before the remote-agents eval suite runs, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a timeout.

Consider a dedicated eval for the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota that alerts when available slots fall below a configurable threshold, providing earlier warning before all capacity is consumed.
